editorial_intro: Pixar brings the toys back after a decade, Bollywood floods the box office with Cocktail 2's four-star opening, and Spielberg's Disclosure Day still rules the multiplex. Add a stone-cold critics' favorite in The Furious and you've got the most loaded weekend of the summer so far.

movies.title: Toy Story 5
movies.why_watch: Woody, Buzz, and the gang are back after more than a decade — and this time the enemy is a screen, not a villain. Pixar's most loaded nostalgia bomb of the year is tracking for one of the biggest animated openings ever. You'll cry harder than the kids.

movies.title: Cocktail 2
movies.why_watch: Fourteen years on, Homi Adajania revives Bollywood's defining urban rom-com — this time with Shahid, Kriti and Rashmika in a messy modern love triangle, and a Pritam soundtrack already on repeat. Critics are calling it a 'WINNER,' and it topped IMDb's most-anticipated list of the year. The diaspora date-night pick of the summer.

movies.title: Disclosure Day
movies.why_watch: Spielberg's first alien movie since War of the Worlds is a government-conspiracy thriller critics are calling his best sci-fi since Close Encounters. It topped the box office on debut and Emily Blunt is already drawing Oscar buzz. Pure big-screen Spielberg.

movies.title: The Furious
movies.rating: Critics' 'Best of the Year' action pick
movies.why_watch: The action film that united critics and fans this year. Choreographer-turned-director Kenji Tanigaki delivers bone-crunching, wall-to-wall combat in the tradition of The Raid. Limited US screens, so hunt it down — it's destined to be a martial-arts cult classic.

movies.title: Main Vaapas Aaunga
movies.why_watch: Imtiaz Ali + A.R. Rahman + Diljit + Naseeruddin Shah in a Partition-era love story spanning 78 years. Naseer's turn as a dementia-stricken patriarch is being called career-defining. Bring tissues — this one lingers.

movies.title: Scary Movie
movies.why_watch: The Wayans brothers reunite the original cast for the first time since 2001 and shattered every franchise record with a $55M domestic opening. It's dumb, it's raunchy, audiences can't get enough. Leave your brain at the door.

movies.title: Backrooms
movies.why_watch: A24's highest-grossing film ever, directed by a 20-year-old YouTube creator. A creepypasta turned liminal nightmare that makes empty hallways and fluorescent lights genuinely terrifying. The internet's horror canon goes mainstream.

movies.title: Obsession
movies.why_watch: Made for under $1M, now past $230M worldwide. A deranged monkey's-paw horror with a star-making turn from Inde Navarrette. The year's biggest box-office Cinderella story is still packing seats.

movies.title: Pressure
movies.why_watch: A D-Day thriller where the battle is over weather forecasts, not beaches. Brendan Fraser as Eisenhower and Andrew Scott as the meteorologist who saved the invasion. CinemaScore: A. A quietly gripping watch.

movies.title: Bandar
movies.why_watch: Anurag Kashyap's grittiest film in years — Bobby Deol strips away all vanity as a fading star caught in India's legal labyrinth. Premiered at TIFF. Not an easy watch, but a powerful one.

movies.title: Welcome To The Jungle
movies.why_watch: The third Welcome film is a full-blown ensemble circus — 25-plus stars, Akshay Kumar back with Ahmed Khan after 19 years, and the kind of loud, all-out comedy that plays best in a packed diaspora theater. Switch your brain off and laugh.

movies.title: Supergirl
movies.why_watch: The DC universe rolls on after Superman. Milly Alcock's hard-living, foul-mouthed Kara Zor-El squares off against Jason Momoa's intergalactic bounty hunter Lobo. Looks wilder and weirder than its predecessor.
